newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end volatile day at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: German shares end volatile day at higher levels.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index rose to within a whisker of the magic 3,800 point level in late trade on Wednesday, with renewed record gains driven by derivatives and with few fundamental reasons for the advance.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade, ended the day at 3,777.56 points, up 47 points or 1.26 percent, having earlier hit a new all-time high of 3,791.31 points.
Earlier its bourse equivalent, the DAX index, ended at 3,749.27 points, up 19 points or 0.51 percent.
The main factor behind the rise was volatility ahead of Friday's "triple-witching" of DAX options, DAX futures and stock options.

"This is mostly options-led, with everyone getting ready for tomorrow -- the index just drops or gains ten points for nothing," a Frankfurt trader said, who said that the volatility combined with a lack of new data was making trading difficult.
Forecasts from the Ifo economic research institute earlier in the day were well received by the market, a trader said.
"They showed that there are no signs of overheating and that there are still signs of growth," he said.
Among the star performers over the day was Volkswagen AG, which ended up 30.50 marks at 1,249 marks, off a high of 1,263.30 marks earlier on.

The group's annual general meeting did not reveal five month figures, as some had expected. The main news to emerge from the meeting was that the carmaker intended to keep up its programme of cost-cutting.

Also performing strongly was the builder Hochtief AG, which ended up nearly six percent, or 4,70 marks at 83.10 marks, amid renewed interest in the construction sector, which has significantly outperformed the MDAX index of medium-sized stocks in recent weeks.
Positive sentiment towards the sector did not extend to builder Philipp Holzmann AG, which was among the afternoon's big losers, down eight marks, 1.60 percent, at 491 marks.
Germany's banks had quite rollercoaster ride because of the options expiry. Deutsche Bank AG ended up 50 pfennigs at 99.34 marks, having earlier fallen to 98.22 marks.
Dresdner Bank AG closed up 70 pfennigs at 61.80 marks, having earlier hit a daily low of 60.60 marks.
